main_body: White porcelain bathtub with a blue water surface, seen from the south and above, with two small feet at the bottom
top_band: Column x=16: white back rim at rows 3-4 (L 236/201), then the blue water surface at rows 5-9 (L 139/180). A white front rim at rows 10-11 (L 228) closes the opening.
evidence: The scan shows a back rim, then a 5-row water surface (rows 5-9), then a light front rim (rows 10-11) that reads as the front edge. Below it the front face steps down in tone (L 201 at row 12, 164 at row 13) with a dark base row at row 14 and the feet beneath. The inside of the opening is clearly visible from above, so it is not a rim-only or front-elevation drawing. The front face is short (about 3 rows plus feet), but that is plausible for a low tub, and the top and front are both clearly drawn. Borderline but passes.

style.evidence: The candidate uses only 10 distinct colours against about 40 and 38 in the references, and its median of 10 colours per tile is below their 17 and 20. The tinted grey-blue outline is fine (0% neutral dark pixels). The white porcelain has about 4-5 steps, but the water is only 2-3 tones with a small highlight patch. There are no grain dots, speckle, scratches or per-part detail. The material ramps are thin and read flatter and simpler than the reference stall and well, so it would look thinner next to them.
